topics: Region locking and data residency constraints
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-17 14:00 PDT · Duration 45m · Attendees: Samir Patel, Claire Nguyen, Dr. Elena Voss, Marco Reis, Priya Shah

[00:00] Samir: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Samir from Redwood, AE on the account. Claire from SE will cover the technical bits. Quick intro please?
[00:12] Dr. Voss: Elena Voss, CISO at Aquila. We run a mix of patient facing web and batch analytics, so data residency and key custody are the big ones for us.
[00:20] Marco: Marco Reis, cloud architect. We're mostly on GCP in us-central1 and europe-west4.
[00:24] Priya: Priya Shah, legal. I'll be focused on BYOK terms and cross-border clauses.
[00:30] Claire: Hi, Claire Nguyen, solutions engineer at Redwood. Today we'll focus on the cryptographic handshake, key custody options, and how audit logs and RBAC tie in.

[02:00] Samir: To start, can you confirm the high level requirement? My reading was: customer-managed keys, HSM-backed, no plaintext data leaving region, audit trail into your SIEM, and SSO for operators. Is that right?
[02:14] Dr. Voss: Yes, exactly. We need tenant keys in our KMS preferably HSM backed, audit logs forwarded to Splunk, and we want a guarantee that the model service won't replicate patient data to other regions.
[02:30] Marco: Also latency constraints: anything that adds >10ms per request on average will be hard for real-time triage workflows.

[04:10] Claire: Understood. Quick overview of options: 1) Hosted with envelope encryption and Redwood-managed KEK; 2) Hosted with BYOK where you import or link your Cloud KMS/HSM and we do envelope encryption; 3) Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment where the control plane is customer-managed and keys never leave your environment. Each has tradeoffs with latency, operational burden, and auditability.
[04:45] Dr. Voss: We're leaning to BYOK or Private. BYOK if your connector keeps keys in GCP HSM, Private if we need full network isolation.

[06:00] Marco: Can you walk through the BYOK flow? Specifically, does Redwood hold any key material? How does signing for streaming tokens work?
[06:14] Claire: For our BYOK connector, Redwood never stores your plaintext KEK. We perform envelope encryption: service data keys (DEKs) are generated per session, encrypted with your KEK via Cloud KMS or HSM using asymmetric wrap/unwrap. We keep wrapped DEKs for short-lived caching in memory; they are re-wrapped on rotation. For signing operations, we support HSM-backed sign/verify via an SRV endpoint—calls are proxied to your KMS HSM. There's a small network RTT to the KMS during unwrap/sign operations unless you use the Private stack colocated with your keys.
[06:55] Marco: Right, so unwraps introduce latency. How often do unwraps happen?
[07:03] Claire: We use a KV cache and prefix caching to avoid frequent unwraps. Typical pattern: we cache decrypted DEKs in memory for the lifespan of a model session; unwraps are on cold start or rotation. For streaming workloads the per-token crypto cost is negligible because we don't unwrap per token. That said, HSM sign operations for attestation will add several ms.

[09:20] Dr. Voss: For compliance we also need the HSM to produce an audit trail of key usage. Does Redwood forward HSM usage logs?
[09:31] Claire: We can forward audit events: unwrap requests, key IDs, operation types, timestamps, and caller identity are pushed to your SIEM via a secure syslog or event stream. Note that the raw HSM audit logs (e.g., vendor-specific tokens) remain in your Cloud KMS audit bucket if you choose BYOK; Redwood will forward standardized events.
[10:00] Priya: And retention? We have contractual requirements: logs retained for 7 years for certain data. Can Redwood store or forward that volume?
[10:10] Samir: We offer long-term archive add-ons—logs can be shipped to your S3/GCS archive with lifecycle policies. We'll need to confirm cost and throughput.

[11:30] Marco: About region lockdown: we must ensure decrypted data or model cache never crosses specified regions. How is that enforced?
[11:42] Claire: Our routing policies let you pin workloads by region. For BYOK, the KMS region must match the serving region; we fail open only to another customer-specified fallback region. For Private VPC, you control the compute region. However, note some ancillary services (control plane metadata, telemetry) may be in our control plane region; we can disable telemetry or forward it under contract.
[12:15] Dr. Voss: Telemetry disabled is preferred unless it's strictly necessary.

[13:40] Marco: If we do Private, what's the onboarding for HSM network connectivity? Firewall rules, mTLS, etc?
[13:52] Claire: We use mutual-TLS for the HSM connector, and recommend a peered VPC with strict firewall egress rules. For on-prem HSMs we provide a connector VM that establishes an outbound-only tunnel to the control plane. For cloud HSMs, we integrate with Cloud KMS via a private endpoint. We can share a connectivity checklist.

[15:30] Priya: Legal question: BYOK import—who is the key custodian? Also escrow options if HSM fails?
[15:40] Samir: With BYOK, you remain the key owner. For import there's two patterns: you either keep keys in your managed KMS (recommended), or you give a wrapped key for temporary systems. For disaster recovery, we support multi-region replication of wrapped DEKs and an escrow process under an NDA where keys can be moved to a cold HSM under customer-approved procedures. We'll document the exact chain of custody.

[17:25] Dr. Voss: Do you support FIPS 140-2/3 validated HSMs and can we require FIPS-only operations?
[17:33] Claire: Yes, our BYOK path is compatible with FIPS validated Cloud HSMs and we can enforce FIPS-only ciphers and restricted TLS profiles. For on-prem FIPS devices, we'll validate the connector with your security team during onboarding.

[19:10] Marco: Small but real concern: signing calls to an external HSM for each session—if that HSM goes down, do we have a fallback?
[19:22] Claire: We support an automated fallback policy that can fail to a standby KMS in the same legal boundary, or to a Redwood-managed key if you opt-in to an emergency escape hatch (requires pre-approval). Otherwise requests will fail closed to preserve security guarantees.

[21:00] Samir: On SSO and RBAC—how will operator access look?
[21:08] Claire: We support SAML/OIDC SSO with SCIM provisioning. RBAC is layered: environment, project, role. Separations of duties—key management ops can be restricted to a small admin group; audit logs show operator identity per action.
[21:45] Priya: We'll need proof of separation for SOC 2. Do you have artifacts?
[21:50] Samir: Yes, we'll share our SOC 2 Type II report and an access control matrix.

[24:00] Marco: Any encryption-at-rest specifics? Do you also encrypt model weights on disk?
[24:10] Claire: Model weights and KV cache are encrypted at rest using per-volume keys; those keys are wrapped with the KEK. Snapshots are encrypted and you can require they remain in region.

[26:30] Dr. Voss: For auditability we want a sample event flow: request -> ingress -> DEK unwrap -> inference -> log push. Can you show that in a runbook?
[26:40] Claire: Yes, we'll provide a sequence diagram and a sample event log.

[28:15] Marco: What about key rotation? We need annual rotation, and rotation should not invalidate long-running sessions.
[28:25] Claire: We do rolling rotation: new KEK used for new DEKs, old DEKs remain valid until TTL expiry; we provide a rotation policy template.

[30:00] Priya: Replay risk and replay-proofing of logs—do you sign logs?
[30:08] Claire: We can forward signed log batches to your archive. Signed manifests and sequencing help detect tampering.

[32:40] Dr. Voss: Any performance numbers we can use to gate a pilot?
[32:46] Claire: We'll run a short bench: 1) Hosted BYOK with GCP HSM in us-central1; 2) Dedicated in us-central1 with HSM proxy; 3) Private VPC same region. We'll measure p99 latency and per-request HSM call breakdown. Expect difference of ~5-25ms depending on HSM unwrap frequency.

[35:00] Samir: Quick commercial notes—BYOK is supported for our hosted tiers; Private requires an enterprise contract. We'll outline pricing for HSM connectors and long-retention logs in the follow-up.

[37:15] Priya: Need to confirm indemnities around cross-border transfer if telemetry is forwarded outside region.
[37:24] Samir: Understood; we'll propose contractual language that forbids telemetry export and offers region-specific control plane options.

[40:00] Claire: I'll follow up with a connectivity checklist, latency test plan, and the event sequence diagram. Samir will send SOC 2/ISO artifacts and the BYOK playbook. Marco will share traffic samples. Priya will send the initial legal redlines.

[42:10] Dr. Voss: That sounds good. If possible, can we queue a 30m deep-dive on Private onboarding next week?
[42:20] Samir: Yes, we'll schedule a Private onboarding deep-dive (SE-led) — propose Wed 2026-09-23 or Thu 2026-09-24.

[44:00] Samir: Thanks everyone. Recap: send artifacts, run bench, legal redlines. We'll sync next week.
[44:10] Marco: Thanks.
[44:12] Priya: Thanks.
[44:15] Claire: Thanks, bye.

Recorded notes: a few transcription artefacts around product names ("Red wood private" in audio) and occasional mis-hear of HSM vendor names. Refer to attachments Samir will send.
